---
title: "How many? (solutions)"
format: html
---

Teacher version. Chunks run. The penguins come with the palmerpenguins package, so no data file is needed.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, palmerpenguins)
```

## The question

How many? One discrete variable, such as the island or the species. We count the rows in each category.

## 1. Count the rows

`count()` gives a table with the number of penguins on each island.

```{r}
#| label: count-island
penguins |>
  count(island)
```

### Your turn 1

Count the penguins of each species.

```{r}
#| label: turn-1
penguins |>
  count(species)
```

Answer: `species`. Adelie has the most penguins, with 152. Chinstrap has 68 and Gentoo has 124.

## 2. The same count as a bar plot

`geom_bar()` counts the rows itself. We only give `x`.

```{r}
#| label: bar-island
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island)) +
  geom_bar()
```

### Your turn 2

Draw the bars of the penguins of each species.

```{r}
#| label: turn-2
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species)) +
  geom_bar()
```

Answer: `species`. The tallest bar is Adelie (152 penguins).

## 3. geom_bar() and geom_col()

The table from section 1 already has the counts. Give it to `geom_bar()` with `y = n` and read the error.

```{r}
#| label: bar-with-y
#| error: true
penguins |>
  count(island) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island, y = n)) +
  geom_bar()
```

`stat_count() must only have an x or y aesthetic`: `geom_bar()` counts rows, and the table has nothing left to count. `geom_col()` draws a number we already have.

```{r}
#| label: col-island
penguins |>
  count(island) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island, y = n)) +
  geom_col()
```

The picture is the same. The reverse mistake, `geom_col()` without `y`, gives `geom_col() requires the following missing aesthetics: y`.

```{r}
#| label: col-no-y
#| error: true
penguins |>
  count(island) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island)) +
  geom_col()
```

### Your turn 3

Draw the species counts with `geom_col()`.

```{r}
#| label: turn-3
penguins |>
  count(species) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = n)) +
  geom_col()
```

Answer: `n`. The picture equals the bars of Your turn 2.

## 4. Color by a second variable

`fill = species` splits each island bar by species.

```{r}
#| label: fill-species
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar()
```

### Your turn 4

Draw the bars of the species, with one color for each island.

```{r}
#| label: turn-4
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, fill = island)) +
  geom_bar()
```

Answer: `island`. Chinstrap lives on Dream only and Gentoo lives on Biscoe only. Adelie lives on all three islands.

## 5. Female and male penguins by island

`fill = sex` splits each island bar by sex. Read the grey segment.

```{r}
#| label: fill-sex
penguins |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar()
```

The grey segment is `NA`: 11 penguins have no sex (Biscoe 5, Dream 1, Torgersen 5). `filter(!is.na(sex))` removes them.

```{r}
#| label: fill-sex-filter
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar()
```

Stacked bars make females and males hard to compare, because the top segment does not start at zero. `position = "dodge"` puts the bars side by side.

```{r}
#| label: dodge
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = island, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge")
```

### Your turn 5

Draw the females and males in each species, side by side.

```{r}
#| label: turn-5
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge")
```

Answer: `species` and `dodge`. The numbers are nearly equal: Adelie 73 and 73, Chinstrap 34 and 34, Gentoo 58 females and 61 males.

## Notes for the teacher

- Counts by island: Biscoe 168, Dream 124, Torgersen 52. By species: Adelie 152, Chinstrap 68, Gentoo 124.
- The two error chunks use `#| error: true`, so the file renders with the errors visible.
- 11 penguins have no sex: Adelie 6, Gentoo 5. Females and males by island: Biscoe 80 and 83, Dream 61 and 62, Torgersen 24 and 23.
- If time runs short, section 5 becomes homework.
